title: 2-Approximation Conjecture for Cluster-VD
statement_text: Cluster-VD can be 2-approximated in polynomial time.
context_text: Given a graph $G$ and a cost function $c:V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_+$, the cluster vertex deletion problem (Cluster-VD) asks for a minimum-cost set $X$ of vertices such that every component of $G-X$ is a complete graph, equivalently such that $G-X$ has no induced $P_3$ (path on three vertices); the conjecture concerns arbitrary nonnegative weights. Being a special case of vertex cover in a 3-uniform hypergraph, it has a straightforward 3-approximation, and You, Wang and Cao gave a $5/2$-approximation for the unweighted version. Adding a pendant edge at every vertex reduces Vertex Cover to Cluster-VD, so it is UGC-hard (hard assuming Khot's Unique Games Conjecture) to approximate Cluster-VD within any ratio better than 2, which makes 2 the natural target. The authors give a $9/4$-approximation algorithm based on the local ratio technique, and observe that it is in fact a 2-approximation on $K_5$-free graphs, and can be adapted to a 2-approximation on diamond-free graphs (the diamond is $K_4$ minus an edge), which supports the conjecture. By contrast, deleting vertices to destroy all triangles is UGC-hard to approximate within a ratio better than 3 (Guruswami and Lee).
notes: Stated in prose in both the abstract and the introduction without a labelled conjecture environment; language is unambiguously conjectural ('We further conjecture that …').
